People  think  success  is  like  watching  a 
 marathon,  not  running  a  marathon.  When 
 you  watch  a  marathon,  you  look  at  the 
 beginning  and  you  look  at  the  end.  But 
 running  a  marathon  is  four,  five,  six 
 straight  hours  of  breathing  heavy, 
 starting  to  play  games  in  your  mind  of 
 like,  "Okay,  I'm  I'm  two-thirds  of  the 
 way  there.  I'm  only  1/5  of  the  of  1/8  of 
 the  way  there."  And  you  keep  doing  this 
 to  play  tricks  on  your  mind  to  keep 
 going.  In  a  mile  marker  race,  it's  very 
 clear  to  know  how  you're  going  to  get  to 
 the  finish  line  and  how  long  it's  going 
 to  take.  The  only  difference  with 
 success  is  that  you  just  have  to  keep 
 running  and  you  don't  know  where  the 
 finish  line  is.
